clue.text: Took part of his mixed salad with main course?

indicators.note: something mixed has been stirred about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: to side with someone is to take their part
the three letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone helped themselves to part of a friend's tossed salad served alongside the main meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took part of his' reads as a single phrase about eating, but it splits into a verb phrase and the fodder for a mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad served with the main course is an example of an accompaniment, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Satchel trimmed and refashioned as a little bag

indicators.note: refashioned means made into a new shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
trimmed means cut short, so the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written, a school bag

explanation.surface: A schoolbag cut down and remade into a small pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet or pouch, a little bag of sugar, shampoo or scent.

clue.text: Succeeded in dreadful couple's ruin

indicators.note: one letter sits in the middle of the following adjective, placed inside it

parts.note: dire means dreadful
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
a couple is a pair; the 's is read as 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a couple whose success went to dreadful ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' looks like the start of the sentence's story, but it is only the single-letter abbreviation used in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is a state of dilapidation, the condition of a building gone to ruin.

clue.text: Study waste that's powdery

indicators.note: to waste is to lay in ruins, so the letters of the word before it are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A neglected study gathers fine dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusty is covered with or resembles fine powder, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Forced fellows taking drug to hide in stables

indicators.note: something hidden in a place sits inside it, so these letters go within the word for stables

parts.note: a stud is an establishment where horses are kept and bred
F is fellow, doubled for the plural
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Men stashing narcotics in horse stables.
explanation.walkthrough: A stud is a place where horses are kept for breeding, so 'stables' is a fair stand-in; the drug is ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced and stuffed both mean crammed or pushed in, as food is forced or stuffed into a turkey.

clue.text: Revels in loutish leader being bitten by animals

indicators.note: a thing bitten is gripped between jaws, so this letter sits inside the word for the animals

parts.note: goats are animals

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the adjective is used

parts.note: the first letter of loutish

explanation.surface: A yob gets nipped by farmyard animals and someone enjoys it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloat is to revel in or relish one's own success or another's misfortune.

clue.text: Night owl passed on part of flight

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died
a riser is the vertical part of each step in a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A nocturnal bird missed part of its flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night owl' and 'flight' suggest a bird in the air, but the flight is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl stays up late and so tends to get up late in the morning, a late riser.

clue.text: Shock to see Dad engaged in lap dance

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
to be engaged in something is to be occupied within it, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: these three letters, rearranged
pa is a word for father

explanation.surface: It would horrify you to see your father performing in a strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: PA goes into the rearranged letters as AP-PA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, the same as to shock someone.

clue.text: Son worked entire year to find peace of mind

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters of the next word are reworked into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
these six letters, rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A boy toiled for a whole year to achieve inner calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is calm untroubled tranquillity, which is what peace of mind amounts to.

clue.text: Gets rid of mould that's revolting to us

indicators.note: revolting means rising up and overturning order, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

parts.note: to cast is to mould, as in metal; the 's after 'that' is read as 'is', so the verb takes its s
these four letters rearranged; the S joins the verb before

explanation.surface: Someone throws away mouldy food that disgusts us.
explanation.walkthrough: CAST (mould) is followed by TO US rearranged as SOUT; 'mould' looks like fungus but is the verb meaning shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast out is to expel or throw away, the same as getting rid of something.

clue.text: Goes off in retirement to embrace happy lethargy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the outer letters wrap around the word for happy
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for goes off is read in the backward direction

parts.note: food that goes off rots
up can mean cheerful, in high spirits

explanation.surface: A pensioner sinks into a contented torpor.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word is split ST-OR around UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or dazed torpor, an extreme lethargy.

clue.text: Area unknown on summit of Everest

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns
taken as written

indicators.note: the summit is the top, and the top of a word in a down light is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Everest

explanation.surface: An uncharted region at the top of the world's highest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or area set apart by some characteristic.

clue.text: Lament variable online support going forward

indicators.note: going forward means moving to the front, so the later words are placed ahead of the variable

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail
a leg supports a table or chair
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans fluctuating internet help in corporate jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going forward' is the business cliché for 'from now on'; here it moves E and LEG in front of Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or song, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Diagram of building gets female toilet right by design

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
loo is British slang for toilet
R is the abbreviation for right
a design is a plan

explanation.surface: An architect's drawing deliberately puts a ladies' lavatory in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor plan is a scale drawing of the layout of rooms in a building, seen from above.

clue.text: Stuck with improvised music

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wedged fast, unable to move

definitions.note: a participle phrase: having played improvised music
definitions.meaning: second meaning: played in a jam session, improvising with other musicians

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in an endless jazz jam session.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer can be wedged immovably, and musicians who improvise together are said to have had a jam session.

clue.text: Small animal's come round to exploit house/burrow of another

indicators.note: to come round something is to go around it, so the animal's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: a mole is a small burrowing animal; the 's is read as 'has'
to exploit something is to use it
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A tiny creature moves into another animal's home to take advantage of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash marks where the wordplay ends and the definition begins; the burrow belongs to a different small animal from the one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousehole is the small hole a mouse lives in, a burrow belonging to an animal other than the mole.

clue.text: I see a devious way that's least effort

definitions.note: the answer means requiring least effort

indicators.note: devious means winding and not straightforward, so the letters before it take a twisted order

parts.note: these five letters, rearranged
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone spots a crafty shortcut that saves the most work.
explanation.definitionFit: The easiest option is the one that demands the smallest amount of effort, the superlative of easy.

clue.text: Test copier after template lost last two letters

indicators.note: losing the final pair of letters means the word is cut short by two at its end
after means following, so the word for copier is placed behind the shortened template

parts.note: an example is a model or template to follow
an aper is one who apes, a copier

explanation.surface: Checking a photocopier after a document template lost its final characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copier' looks like an office machine, but it is a person who imitates.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam paper is the set of questions given in a written test.

clue.text: Makes better-produced movies getting to grips with marketing

indicators.note: produced means staged or put together, so the letters of the next word are arranged anew
to get to grips with something is to grasp it, so the rearranged letters hold the marketing abbreviation

parts.note: these six letters, rearranged
PR is public relations, promotion and marketing

explanation.surface: Better-made films are those that take marketing seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'better-produced' joins the definition to the anagram indicator to mislead; PR goes in as IM-PR-OVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something is to make it better, so improves is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Nobleman in France who admitted to spreading MRSA

indicators.note: spreading means scattering about, as an infection does, so the four letters are rearranged
something admitted to a place is let inside it, so the French word goes within the other letters

parts.note: the four letters of the hospital superbug's name, rearranged
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat confesses to spreading a hospital superbug.
explanation.walkthrough: MRSA is a drug-resistant bacterium; QUI goes in as MAR-QUI-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl or count and below a duke.

clue.text: Winter transport needs tail light…

indicators.note: the tail is the hindmost part, so only the end letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of needs
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: A winter vehicle needs a rear lamp, the ellipsis carrying on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail light' reads as a rear lamp, but tail works on needs and light stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled is a vehicle on runners for travelling over snow, so it is transport for winter.

clue.text: Impound fuel-guzzling luxury car

indicators.note: something guzzling swallows greedily, so the fuel word takes the car inside it

parts.note: coal is a fuel
RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker

explanation.surface: Police seize a gas-guzzling limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel-guzzling' looks like one adjective, but the hyphen hides a noun and a container indicator: CO-RR-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To corral is to shut animals in a pen, so it means to impound or confine.

clue.text: …yet case made for road lighting

indicators.note: made means constructed, so the letters of the words before it are built into a new order

parts.note: these seven letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a case is being made for lighting roads.
explanation.walkthrough: Catseyes are reflective studs set into British road surfaces to mark lanes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A catseye is a reflector stud in the road that shines in headlights, a form of road lighting.

clue.text: Beaten hollow, teams return in buzzer round at the end

indicators.note: in places the reversed pair inside the word for buzzer

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing insect

indicators.note: to return is to come back, so the kept pair are read backwards
hollow means emptied out, so only the outside letters of the word that follows are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of teams

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of round

explanation.surface: A quiz team is thrashed in the buzzer round at the end of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten hollow' looks like one phrase meaning soundly defeated; only Beaten is the definition. The reversed pair goes in as BE-ST-E, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to defeat them, so bested means beaten.

clue.text: Artist's opening with installation of endless trees, an exceptional thing

indicators.note: installing something fits it into place, so these letters are put inside the artist's opening

parts.note: RA is Royal Academician, an artist; the 's is possessive
a vent is an opening

indicators.note: endless means with no ends, so both outside letters are dropped and the inside is kept

parts.note: the middle letters of trees

explanation.surface: A gallery opening features an installation of trees cut short, something truly unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' and 'installation' suggest an art exhibition, but they work as a noun for a gap and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare event is something that seldom happens, an exceptional occurrence.

clue.text: Surprises with diamonds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shakes or stuns someone
second meaning: slang for gems, especially diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone springs a proposal with a diamond ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock rocks a person, and rocks is informal slang for diamonds or other precious stones.

clue.text: Regret pinching exercise class money

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing between fingers, so the word for regret grips the class letters

parts.note: to rue is to regret
PE is physical education, a school exercise class

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans stealing the cash for the gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and other countries, so it is money.

clue.text: They slow down bachelor leaving with libertines

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the bachelor's letter departs from the word

parts.note: brakes slow a vehicle down
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees

explanation.surface: A bachelor who goes off with womanisers will soon calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man of fashion, an old-fashioned word for a libertine.

clue.text: Champion's in charge during comeback set, getting gold

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the in-charge letters sit within the other word
a comeback is a return, so the word for set is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a TV set
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A tennis star leads during a comeback set and wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' and 'comeback' suggest tennis, but the set is a television. Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is the winner of a contest, so a champion.

clue.text: Take seven days reportedly to notice flaw

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: seven days make a week, which sounds the same as the adjective for feeble
to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: It takes a week to find a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak spot is a point of vulnerability or a failing, a flaw in something.

clue.text: Model's wearing messy ensemble for routine

indicators.note: an ensemble is things assembled together, so the letters of the word before it are put together anew
something wearing clothes is inside them, so the model's letter sits within the rearranged letters

parts.note: these five letters, rearranged
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A fashion model wears a scruffy outfit for a catwalk routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messy ensemble' reads as an untidy outfit, but messy is the fodder and ensemble the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a regular method or procedure, the same as a routine way of doing things.

clue.text: Decided to fill alcoholic drink to a preset level

indicators.note: filling something goes into it, so the word for decided goes inside the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
decided in the sense of certain, sure

explanation.surface: A barman decides to top up a drink exactly to the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decided' looks like a verb, but here it is the adjective meaning certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something measured has been gauged to an exact predetermined quantity, as a measured dose is.
